The year in the apiary

A guide only: it varies with region and weather.

Spring

The colony grows fast.

  • Frequent inspections
  • Add space
  • Watch for swarming

Summer

Heat, nectar and harvest.

  • Water nearby
  • Honey harvest
  • Shade and airflow

Autumn

Getting ready for winter.

  • Check stores
  • Health control
  • Narrow the entrance

Winter

The colony clusters.

  • Open as little as possible
  • Check the weight
  • Prepare equipment

Before you come: stings and allergies

Stings can happen even in a suit. If you have had an allergic reaction or have any doubt, ask your doctor before enrolling and tell us. If you have trouble breathing, a swollen face or throat, or feel faint after a sting, call 112.

Questions

Do I need my own hives?

No. Beginners practise in the school apiary.

Is equipment lent?

Yes, during practical sessions (sample condition).

What should I wear?

Long clothing, high socks and closed boots. Avoid perfume.

Do hives need to be registered?

There are registration and distance rules in Spain. Check those of your region and town; the course gives guidance.

What if it rains?

The practical is rescheduled, as hives are not opened in bad weather.
